content.text:
The Takeout import finished successfully. It processed all 9 files and added 11 records, with no updates or duplicates.

**Does this connect your API account? No.** Importing a Takeout archive only loads the local database from the file. The connection check shows no verified connection for either Google or Fitbit. If you want live API access, that needs a separate connection step.

**Coverage is very thin.** Each metric covers one or two days:

| Source | Category | Metric | Dates |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fitbit | Activity | Steps (2 records) | Oct 1, 2026 |
| Fitbit | Body | BMI | Oct 1, 2026 |
| Fitbit | Body | Weight | Oct 1, 2026 |
| Fitbit | Heart | Heart rate (samples) | Oct 1, 2026 |
| Fitbit | Heart | Resting heart rate | Oct 1, 2026 |
| Fitbit | Sleep | Efficiency, minutes asleep, minutes awake, time in bed | Oct 2, 2026 |
| Google | Activity | Steps | Oct 3, 2026 |

Everything else (exercise, SpO2, nutrition, cardio fitness, ECG, and others) has no local records.

**Caveats:**
- Weight has an unknown unit, so it is excluded from unit-converted summaries.
- One day in the resting heart rate file had no estimate and was treated as missing, not zero.
- Three files were not parsed: a sleep log CSV, an HTML file, and a JSON file with an unrecognized structure. A symbolic link in the archive was also skipped. These are kept on disk.
- Because each metric has only a day or two of data, trends or summaries from this import would not be meaningful.
